newsitem.title: GERMANY: Suu Kyi urges German business to avoid Burma.
newsitem.headline: Suu Kyi urges German business to avoid Burma.

text.p: Burmese democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi, the 1991 Nobel Peace laureate, on Wednesday urged German companies to shelve plans to open an investment office in Rangoon, German broadcaster Deutsche Welle reported.

The business center planned by eight German companies including Deutsche Telekom AG, ABB, and Dresdner Bank AG would not help democracy in Burma, Suu Kyi was quoted saying in a statement from the broadcaster.

"We're not in favour of investment in Burma at this particular moment because money that gets into the country does not get to the people that need it most ... (New investments) would only enrich an already very rich elite," she said.

Foreign investment has been a focal point of Burmese government efforts to revive the economy, but Suu Kyi has urged foreigners not to invest until Burma improves its human rights record and starts talks with the democracy movement.

Renewed outbreaks of student unrest and bombings in recent weeks have prompted fears that foreign investors could move to the sidelines, waiting to see if they were isolated acts or part of a bigger campaign.
The German investment office is due to be opened on January 30 by a visiting delegation of 15 business representatives.

Wolfgang Niedermark, regional manager of the German Asia-Pacific Business Association, told Deutsche Welle the Rangoon office would help put German companies in contact with potential Burmese partners.
Niedermark said he was aware of political tensions, but that foreign investment could help bring change in Burma, and is preferable to isolation or investment boycotts.
Suu Kyi said, "If I could persuade them to cancel their plans, I would do so ... Perhaps the German public should persuade them not to go ahead."
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel last week condemned restrictions imposed on Suu Kyi by the Burmese government and said they were an "attempt to hold on to dictatorial power".
German trade with Burma amounted to around $50 million in 1994.
